html:
The last land battle of the Persian invasion of Greece, fought near Plataea in Boeotia in August 479 BCE. A Greek army led by Sparta destroyed the Persian army left behind by Xerxes.

After the Greek naval win at Salamis in 480 BCE, Xerxes went home but left his general Mardonius with a large army. Spartans, Athenians and many other cities gathered under the Spartan regent Pausanias. After days of skirmishes, the Greeks were withdrawing in some disorder when the Persians attacked. Spartan hoplites held, Mardonius was killed, and his army broke.

Tradition says that on the same day the Greek fleet beat the Persians at Mycale, in Asia Minor. Persia never again invaded mainland Greece. The Greeks set up a bronze column of three twisted snakes at Delphi with the names of the cities that fought; it now stands in Istanbul. Soon after, Athens formed the Delian League to carry the war to Persia. Herodotus is the main source.
sum: The last land battle of the Persian invasion of Greece, fought near Plataea in Boeotia in August 479 BCE. A Greek army led by Sparta destroyed the Persian army left behind by Xerxes.
